normalized.governing_thought: Partner with RouteSprout in 2027 instead of buying it on the proposed terms, and keep a staged, ARR-priced purchase that diligence must earn
executive_summary: The proposed $18M all-cash deal breaks the cash floor and pays back only on the sellers' assumptions – Price plus integration leaves $2M of cash, $7M below the floor – It covers its costs only if cross-sell reaches $2.3M, 96% of an unsigned plan (p. 4–7)

RouteSprout's customers are less stable than the pitch assumes, so integration must protect renewals – Logo churn rose from 12% to 21%, and 41 accounts hold 58% of ARR – A full migration uses the whole $4M integration cap, with 30% unscoped (p. 9–11)

Of the four paths, only the partnership meets the board's cash, timing and continuity tests in 2027 – The staged deal clears the floor at signing, then falls below it within a year – The partnership costs a $1.2M minimum and delivers routing this summer (p. 13–15)

Keep buying as an option: run diligence alongside the partnership, then buy only on staged terms – Upfront cash must stay below about $8.4M, about 1.8 times ARR – The board decides at a Q4 2027 gate; if diligence fails, the partnership continues (p. 17–20)

slides.title: The customer base behind the price
RouteSprout's base is getting less stable: logo churn reached 21%, while a few large accounts hold 58% of ARR

claims.claim: Churn has almost doubled in two years
evidence: Logo churn FY2024 12%; FY2026 21%

claims.claim: A small group of accounts carries most of the revenue
evidence: 58% of ARR comes from 41 of 310 accounts
$2.8M of ARR rides on those 41 renewals
Those 41 accounts are 13% of the customer base
No customer-level churn cohort shows whether they are the ones leaving

claims.claim: Any integration that unsettles the 41 largest accounts puts more than half of RouteSprout's ARR at risk
evidence: Seller-reported figures; no customer-level churn cohort or independently verified ARR schedule exists yet

slides.title: The 95% renewal of routing users reflects who those customers are, not what routing does for them

claims.claim: The 95% renewal of routing users reflects who those customers are, not what routing does for them
evidence: Renewal rate: Routing users 95%; Smaller customers without routing 78%
Routing users: mostly larger, multi-branch companies with dedicated customer-success teams
Smaller customers without routing: differ in size and support as well as in the feature, so the gap does not isolate routing
What drives renewal: customer-success interviews point to account managers, not routing features alone
The sales deck concludes "routing causes retention"; the comparison does not control for customer size or support model

claims.claim: No retention uplift belongs in the deal value
Value the deal without a retention uplift, and keep account managers in place through any integration

slides.title: An API-first link protects renewals better than a six-month full migration that uses the whole $4M integration cap

claims.claim: An API-first link protects renewals better than a six-month full migration that uses the whole $4M integration cap
evidence: Scope: Full migration – All customer records and support operations moved; assumes zero change-management delay | API-first – Products linked by API and single sign-on; RouteSprout's interface kept
Integration cost: $4M | Simpler, per the Integration Director; not yet costed
Work not yet scoped: 30% | Smaller scope to define and audit before signing
Customer change: Interface replaced, possibly before the largest accounts renew | Large customers keep the screens they renew on
Uptime: Migration cut-overs put the 99.7% uptime target at risk; credits are not in the sellers' case | Fewer cut-overs to test against the uptime target
Evidence it works: Sellers cite peers twice RouteSprout's size with lower churn; correlation only | Matches the product VP's concern about churn at renewal

claims.claim: If the unscoped 30% is extra, integration reaches about $5.7M ($4M ÷ 70%), over the cap
evidence: The board caps one-time integration spend at $4M through 2028; a missed quarterly uptime target triggers service credits and renewal risk

slides.title: Four routing paths compared
The staged deal clears the cash floor at signing, but a year of RouteSprout losses would push Atlas below it

evidence: Cash after initial spend: A · Full deal 2; B · Staged deal 9.5; C · Partnership 22.8; D · Build 20.6 ($M); Board cash floor $9.0M
Staged deal: cash after a year of losses and support, before cross-sell $7.7M ($9.5M − $1.85M a year)
Staged deal: gap to the floor after that year −$1.4M ($7.65M − $9M floor)
Initial spend: A $18M + $4M; B $11M + $3.5M; C $1.2M two-year minimum; D $3.4M through 2028. Atlas's own operations assumed cash-break-even

evidence: A · Full deal: below the floor from day one
B · Staged deal: the earnout of up to $7M falls due in 2029, after the cushion has been drawn down

slides.title: On the board's four tests, the partnership is the strongest 2027 path and the full acquisition the weakest

claims.claim: On the board's four tests, the partnership is the strongest 2027 path and the full acquisition the weakest
evidence: A · Full deal: $22M; Reject: breaks the floor; no payback in the base case
B · Staged deal: $14.5M; Not as offered; only restructured, after diligence
C · Partnership: $1.2M; Do in 2027; limits: nonexclusive, 45% of gross profit to RouteSprout
D · Build: $3.4M; Reject: late 2028 at best, displaces compliance work
Partnership payback: Atlas keeps about 44% of each routing dollar as gross profit (80% × 55%), so about $2.7M of revenue over two years recovers the minimum
Founders want to sell and the API is nonexclusive: add change-of-control protection

slides.title: An in-house build would add only about $0.64M a year, and not before late 2028

claims.claim: An in-house build would add only about $0.64M a year, and not before late 2028
evidence: $1.3M 2028 ARR if the build launches on time (product head) × 80% incremental gross margin − $0.4M annual operations after launch = $0.6M annual contribution from launch

claims.claim: The build is slower and riskier than the partnership on four counts
evidence: Engineers need at least 18 months for a basic product, so launch comes no earlier than late 2028; a partner could ship a limited offer this summer
At $0.64M a year, the $3.4M build takes about 5.3 years after launch to pay back, a best case given the late launch
The effort displaces a planned compliance upgrade, whose delay has a customer cost not yet estimated
Only one major routing strategy is allowed in 2027, so building rules out the partnership for the year

slides.title: A conditional path to buying
Five pieces of missing evidence decide whether buying RouteSprout later is worth doing at all

claims.claim: Five pieces of missing evidence decide whether buying RouteSprout later is worth doing at all
evidence: Churn cohort and renewal dates: Whether the 21% logo churn hits the 41 largest accounts, and when they renew → Churn in large accounts: walk away
Verified ARR schedule: Whether the $4.8M holds once pilots and multi-year value are stripped out → Lower ARR: cut the price in proportion
Signed cross-sell pipeline: How much of the $2.4M base case is actually contracted → The deciding test / The deal breaks even only at about $2.3M of cross-sell ARR
Audited integration budget: Whether the unscoped 30% and integration-era support fit under the $4M cap → Over the cap: API-first scope only, or no deal
Key people retention: Whether key engineers commit to two years and account managers stay → No commitments: the product's value falls away
None of the five exists today: the board has offered to approve preliminary due diligence before committing to a deal

slides.title: To keep Atlas above its floor through a year of losses, upfront cash must stay below about $8.4M

claims.claim: To keep Atlas above its floor through a year of losses, upfront cash must stay below about $8.4M
evidence: $15M spendable cash above the $9M floor − $1.2M partnership minimum, paid first − $3.5M integration, staged plan − $1.9M a year of loss and support = $8.4M maximum upfront payment

claims.claim: The ceiling rests on four assumptions to test in diligence
evidence: Integration stays at $3.5M; unscoped work lowers the ceiling dollar for dollar, and with a year of support it already reaches $4.35M against the $4M cap
RouteSprout's loss stays at $1M a year (including founders' salaries), with no savings and no first-year cross-sell
At the ceiling cash sits on the floor after a year, so the $7M earnout must be funded by the business itself
The ceiling is about 1.8 times recognized ARR, compared with 2.3 times for the $11M staged offer

slides.title: Next steps

normalized.recommendation: Partner with RouteSprout in 2027 instead of buying it on the proposed terms, and keep a staged, ARR-priced purchase that diligence must earn. Approve the RouteSprout partnership as Atlas's single 2027 routing strategy and fund preliminary due diligence; run diligence alongside the partnership, then buy only on staged terms (upfront cash below about $8.4M, about 1.8 times ARR), with a go / no-go at the Q4 2027 board for closing in 2028; if diligence fails, the partnership continues.

alternatives_considered.option: A · Full deal ($18M all-cash acquisition plus $4M integration)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Reject: breaks the floor; no payback in the base case. Leaves $2M of cash, $7M below the $9M floor; nets only $0.07M a year in the base case.

alternatives_considered.option: B · Staged deal ($11M upfront + $3.5M integration, earnout up to $7M)
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not as offered; only restructured, after diligence. Clears the floor at signing ($9.5M) but a year of losses pushes cash to $7.7M, −$1.4M below the floor; earnout falls due in 2029.
Do in 2027; limits: nonexclusive, 45% of gross profit to RouteSprout. Only path meeting the board's cash, timing and continuity tests in 2027; delivers routing this summer.
Reject: late 2028 at best, displaces compliance work. Adds only about $0.64M a year; about 5.3 years after launch to pay back; rules out the partnership for 2027.

alternatives_considered.option: Full migration in six months (sellers' integration plan) vs API and single sign-on first
alternatives_considered.treatment: API-first link protects renewals better than a six-month full migration that uses the whole $4M integration cap; if the unscoped 30% is extra, full migration reaches about $5.7M, over the cap.
